text:
sasha: Quick follow-up on the preflight-proxy operator contract RFC — want to lock down minimal surface and failure modes before we merge. TL;DR: operator should never hold private keys, only attest and request signed artifacts via offline relay.

maya: thanks — can you spell out expected RPC surface? health / reconcile / fetch?

arch: proposed minimal API: GET /health, POST /reconcile {component, version}, POST /fetch-intent {manifest-id}. No auth on /health, mTLS for the others.

jen: +1 on mTLS. We need clear KMS boundaries: operator makes a signed request to the relay, but KMS ops (unwrap) must happen in the relay. Operator never sees signing key material.

tom: edge-case: what about operator running in VERY restricted airgapped env where relay is local but untrusted? We need a fallback for operator to verify signatures itself.

arch: right. Add verification mode: operator has a pinned public root (catalog root) and can verify bundle signatures locally. But it must not attempt to sign anything. Verification-only mode should be explicitly enabled by admin flag.

maya: sounds good. How do we surface that in UX/config? example config snippet?

arch: small example:
```yaml
operator:
  mode: verification-only  # or relay-proxy
  pinned_root: sha256:3f4a...
  relay_endpoint: https://relay.local:8443
  enable_agent_backoff: true
```

jen: one more: rollout safety. If operator fails verification we should not auto-activate partial components. Add a strict-check flag where anything failing verification triggers operator to create a sealed-alert and halt activation until manual ack.

sasha: agree. For automatic upgrades we keep two-stage activation: staged-download -> verify -> activate. If verify fails, operator falls back to last-known-good and emits alert to console + metrics.

tom: note on observability: metrics we need: fetch_duration_seconds, verify_pass_total, verify_fail_total, activation_recover_count. Traces should include manifest-id and operator-mode (relay|verification). Keep PII out.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout started: operator-image v1.5.0 -> arch-lab cluster (3 nodes) :rocket:

maya: any thoughts on backoff/retry semantics for intermittent partial downloads? We should avoid thundering herd when network flakes.

arch: implement jittered exponential backoff with per-manifest token bucket. Default: initial=2s, max=5m, jitter=0.5. If operator is in relay-proxy mode, relay can coordinate a lease to avoid duplicate downloads.

jen: security check: ensure operator logs do not contain manifest payloads or signing material. redact bundle digests in high-verbosity logs.

sasha: decision summary (for the RFC follow-up):
- Operator modes: relay-proxy, verification-only.
- Surface: /health, /reconcile, /fetch-intent; mTLS for control endpoints.
- Keys: signing/unwrap only in relay; operator only verifies with pinned root.
- Activation flow: download -> verify -> activate; strict-check halts activation on verify failures.
- Backoff: jittered exponential + relay lease for canary/coordination.
- Metrics/traces: fetch_duration, verify_pass/fail, activation_recover_count.
- Logging: redact sensitive fields.

tom: fine with me. Will we add a short RFC PR that includes the API stubs + metrics list?

sasha: yes — I'll open PR today and tag @eng-security and @devex for review.

maya: thanks — will run quick tabletop sim on Friday with semi-airgapped VM and report failure-mode gaps.

arch: added note: operator should expose a /liveness that returns details only when queried with admin token to support operator-level forensics (not for automated healthchecks).

jen: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploybot: canary passed health check at 1758887778, promoting to staging.

sasha: awesome — closing thread. If anyone spots anything missing ping me directly.
